prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals a diagonal tabletop plane sloping away from the camera wearer, from the bright near edge and tableware at the bottom-right within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m) to the dimmer far edge (~1.0–1.5 m) and dark background beyond (>2 m). In frames 1 and 2, while the camera looks further down the right side of the table, mid-grey silhouettes show an arm leaning over the far table edge (~1.2–1.4 m ahead) and a partial head/shoulder on the far right (~1.4–1.6 m), both facing toward the table. Across frames 3 to 5, as the viewpoint shifts slightly left, two people seated along the left side of the table (~0.4–0.5 m apart from each other) move into view: a bright, partially cropped person in the lower-left foreground (~0.4–0.6 m, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and touched from behind by an adjacent hand/arm) and a second person just beyond them (~0.8–1.2 m) facing right toward the table with a bent left arm resting near a plate and glass (~0.3 m in front of them) and their head turning slightly toward the camera by frame 5. This map makes the silhouettes, relative distances, and foreground occlusions of the dimly lit people and arms much clearer than the dark RGB frames. However, it is unreliable around the lit candle and glassware in frames 1 and 2, where bright light and reflections produce artificially near blobs, and it smooths over thin utensils and small plates.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map fails to detect the dining table, the far-side diners, and most tableware due to extreme low light, leaving almost the entire scene unsegmented black space. Across the sequence, it sporadically isolates only a few tabletop objects within ~0.5–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer: in frame 1, it correctly labels the near water glass (~0.5 m, within arm's reach) as a 'cup' while misclassifying a bowl to its left (~0.8 m) as a 'mouse' and a small square plate above it (~1.0 m) as a 'book'. As the camera shifts slightly left across frames 2 to 4, it tracks only single isolated items per frame—misclassifying plates (~0.8–1.0 m) as a 'book' in frame 2 and a 'laptop' in frame 3, before correctly labelling the central dark bowl (~0.7 m, within arm's reach) as a 'bowl' in frame 4. In frame 5, it misclassifies the close lower-left person's bare shoulder, back, and an overlapping hand (~0.4–0.6 m, partially cropped at the bottom-left edge) as a green 'chair' mask and a far-right plate (~1.2 m) as a 'book'. While these masks crisply outline the 2D footprints of a few dim plates and bowls that blend into the dark tabletop in RGB, the map is highly unreliable in both object classification and scene completeness, providing almost no information about people's orientations or multi-person layout.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only yellow body skeletons on black with no magenta hand skeletons detected in any frame, and it completely misses all people in frames 2 and 3 as well as the diners across the table (~1.2–1.5 m away). In frame 1, it detects a single horizontally stretched skeleton in the mid-left (~0.8–1.2 m from the camera wearer) near the left edge of the table, and in frame 4 it detects only a compact torso structure in the lower-left foreground (~0.5–0.7 m, within arm's reach). By frame 5, as the left side of the table is more fully in view, it separates the two left-side diners (~0.4–0.5 m apart): an upper-left person (~0.9–1.2 m away) leaning right with head keypoints facing rightward across the table and slightly toward the camera wearer, and a lower-left foreground person (~0.4–0.6 m away, partially out of view at the bottom edge) angled forward and right toward the table. These skeletons help confirm the presence and head-to-shoulder orientation of the dark-adapted figures on the left side that are nearly indistinguishable from the background in RGB. However, the map is spatially unreliable because it drops detections across most frames, misses all hands and far-side arms reaching toward the table settings, and collapses the torso geometry into distorted boxes.
